title: Simultaneous integral lifts of rational cone elements
statement: Let $G$ be an abelian group, let $V$ be a vector space over the rational field $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-field], and let $i:G\to V$ be an injective additive homomorphism. Let $P\subseteq G$ contain $0$ and be closed under addition. Define $C\subseteq V$ to be the set of all finite sums $\sum_j q_ji(p_j)$ with $p_j\in P$ and $q_j\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}$, including the empty sum. For every finite set $T$ and every family $(x_t)_{t\in T}$ of elements of $C$, there are an integer $N\ge1$ and elements $a_t\in P$ such that $i(a_t)=Nx_t$ for every $t\in T$. For every $g\in G$ one has $$i(g)\in C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{there is an integer }n\ge1\text{ such that }ng\in P.$$ If $x,-x\in C$, there exist an integer $N\ge1$ and $a,b\in P$ such that $i(a)=Nx$, $i(b)=-Nx$, and $a+b=0$ in $G$. No finite-generation, saturation or sharpness assumption on $P$ is imposed, and the empty family permits $N=1$.

proof.text: For each $t\in T$, choose a defining expression $x_t=\sum_{j\in J_t}q_{tj}i(p_{tj})$ with $J_t$ finite, $p_{tj}\in P$ and $q_{tj}\ge0$. Write each rational coefficient as $q_{tj}=u_{tj}/d_{tj}$ with $u_{tj}\in\mathbf N$ and $d_{tj}\in\mathbf N_{>0}$. This is the usual numerator-denominator description of a nonnegative rational number; zero permits numerator $0$ and denominator $1$. The set $E=\{(t,j):t\in T,\ j\in J_t\}$ is finite, since it is a finite union of finite sets.

proof.text: Put $N=\prod_{e\in E}d_e$, with empty product $1$. Every factor is positive, so $N\ge1$. For each $e\in E$, put $D_e=\prod_{f\in E\setminus\{e\}}d_f$ and $m_e=u_eD_e\in\mathbf N$. The identity $N=d_eD_e$ gives $Nq_e=(d_eD_e)(u_e/d_e)=m_e$. Thus the same $N$ makes every coefficient in every chosen expression a nonnegative integer.

proof.text: Define $a_t=\sum_{j\in J_t}m_{tj}p_{tj}$, where multiplication in $G$ means repeated addition. Induction on the number of summands shows $a_t\in P$: start with $0\in P$ and repeatedly use addition closure, first for each $m_{tj}p_{tj}$ and then for their sum. Additivity of $i$ and distributivity in $V$ give $i(a_t)=\sum_jm_{tj}i(p_{tj})=\sum_j(Nq_{tj})i(p_{tj})=Nx_t$. This proves the simultaneous-lift assertion. If $T$ is empty, $E$ is empty and $N=1$; if an individual expression is empty its lift is $0$.

source.place: Agent-written elementary expansion of the immediate parent lem-trf-sharp-cone-lattice-intersection, proof steps 4--5. ILO Expose VIII 3.1.17, printed p. 101, and Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, provide saturation and fan context only, not a proof of this assertion.

proof.text: If $i(g)\in C$, apply the simultaneous-lift construction just proved to the singleton family $x=i(g)$. It gives $a\in P$ with $i(a)=Ni(g)=i(Ng)$, the last equality following by repeated additivity. Injectivity of $i$ implies $a=Ng$, hence $Ng\in P$ with $N\ge1$. Conversely, if $ng\in P$ and $n\ge1$, the single term $(1/n)i(ng)=i(g)$ is a defining expression for an element of $C$, since $1/n\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}$. This proves both directions of the equivalence.

proof.text: For $x,-x\in C$, apply the simultaneous-lift construction to a two-element index set, retaining two indices even when $x=0$. It gives one $N\ge1$ and $a,b\in P$ with $i(a)=Nx$ and $i(b)=N(-x)=-Nx$. Then $i(a+b)=i(a)+i(b)=Nx-Nx=0=i(0)$. Injectivity gives $a+b=0$. This uses neither saturation nor sharpness nor finite generation of $P$.

lean.statement: theorem simultaneous_integral_lifts {G : Type u} [AddCommGroup G] {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℚ V] (i : G →+ V) (hi : Function.Injective i) (P : Set G) (h0 : (0 : G) ∈ P) (hadd : ∀ {a b : G}, a ∈ P → b ∈ P → a + b ∈ P) : (∀ (T : Type w) [Fintype T] (x : T → V), (∀ t, x t ∈ hull ℚ (i '' P)) → ∃ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N ∧ (IsEmpty T → N = 1) ∧ ∃ a : T → G, ∀ t, a t ∈ P ∧ i (a t) = (N : ℚ) • x t) ∧ (∀ g : G, i g ∈ hull ℚ (i '' P) ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ n • g ∈ P) ∧ (∀ x : V, x ∈ hull ℚ (i '' P) → -x ∈ hull ℚ (i '' P) → ∃ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N ∧ ∃ a b : G, a ∈ P ∧ b ∈ P ∧ i a = (N : ℚ) • x ∧ i b = (N : ℚ) • (-x) ∧ a + b = 0)
